page.layout: One block of text in a single column, with the page number at the top right. Above the text, a printed woodcut ornament. Headings at the top of the column: "LIBER IIII.", "CANTICA SACRA.", "CANTICVM MOSIS." and "Ex cap. 15. Exodi." Then the verse in stanzas, followed by the signature at the foot right. No marginal notes, no running head.

main_text.head: LIBER IIII.
CANTICA SACRA.
CANTICVM MOSIS.
Ex cap. 15. Exodi.
main_text.p: LAudemus Dominum, cuius virtute profundis Equites, & ipsi sunt[?] equi immersi vadis. Ille mea vires, mea magna potentia solus, Meisque semper digna versibus seges. Nempe salutifero me tutum numine servas[?] Ab impotentis hostis inclementia. Ergo erit ille mihi semper Deus, illius unum Sonare nomen me lyra dulci iuvat: Ille mea gentis patrius Deus, illius alto Efferre Caelo cantibus laudes lubet. Bellipotens, fortisque, Iouæ cui nobile nomen, In belluosum tota proiecit Salum Agminaque & currus Pharaonis, & inclyta gentis[?] Nomina, regendis copiis lectos Duces. Qui rubri absorpti sinuosis æquoris undis, Vt missa ad imum saxa nunc fundum iacent. Magne Parens, valido iuncta tu robore dextra Virtutis amplum specimen hic praebes tuae! Magne Parens, valido inuicta tu robore dextra Fregisti inanes victor aduersarios.

page.notes: Printed "LAudemus" begins with a woodcut initial L. "ipsi sunt" is set with a worn "sut"; read as "sunt" with [?]. A printer's dingbat follows "servas" in the printed line; the word is marked [?]. "Iouæ" and "gentis" are worn in print and marked [?]. "iuncta" is read from a worn ligature. The faint show-through at the top of the page is not transcribed.
